# Three Coven Lake · Book II, pp. 438–447
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	438
P	Deep in the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372) lies a large lake, eight miles long by three. The waters are murky, often choppy, shallow in some places, in others 100 feet deep.
P	Rocky islands poke from the water. Bluffs line much of the shore. But look closer.
P	Those islands are the feet of ancient towers, and those bluffs are riddled with rockcut rooms. For long ago, in the days of the <b>Stone Lords</b> (page 382), this was a mighty city. Teirstered, they called it. The City of Three Stars, rivalled only by great <b>Dulenn</b> (page 48).
P	Picture it! See it in your mind! The stone and crystal spires, rising from the lake.
P	Their glowing tips of <b>makerglass</b> (page 388), shining in the night. The walkways, stretched between the towers, so that one might walk the valley's length without ever setting foot on shore.
P	Those walkways were more than just convenience. They formed a mighty rune, a seal that helped to bind the power of the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412). The ceaseless march of countless feet powered the rune, like how water turns a wheel.
P	When the Stone Lords' servants rebelled, they sank the city of Dulenn in one night.
P	But here, in Teirstered, things took longer.
P	Mobs rose up against their masters and besieged them in their towers. They broke the walkways, called up horrors from the deep. Towers swayed, then crumbled, then fell beneath the waves.
P	Soon, the city lay in ruins. But it was not abandoned. The <b>Barrow Builders</b> (page 34) fought over its bones. They sought the treasures of their fallen masters, and to seat themselves upon their thrones.
P	Their armies spilled each others' blood. The waters drank it up.
P	In time, there was little left to fight over.
P	In time, the Things Below withdrew. The tyrants of the Barrow Builders were cast down, or imprisoned, or left alone to rot.
P	Teirstered, the City of Three Stars, was no more.
P	But the blood-drunk waters of Three
P	Coven Lake remained.
PAGE	439
H2	Impressions
HR
B	So… much… water… (gulp)
B	Calm water: reflections of the bluffs
B	Choppy water: cold and dark, the angry churn and spray
B	Broken buildings, glimpsed beneath the water
B	Echoes off the bluffs: waves, voices, birdcalls, mournful screeches
B	At night: motes of light in the deep
B	When chilly: fog—thick, wet, gloomy
B	In winter: a white expanse, frozen solid, windy, slick, snow-covered
H2	The Three Covens
P	Three lights can be seen every night, like ghostly flames: one among the northern bluffs, one on the south shore, the third upon (below?) the waters. <b>Hillfolk</b> (page 228) call them "the Covens" or the "the Witch Lights." They hesitate to say more.
P	Who or what are the Covens? That's for you to decide. But perhaps they…
E	burn in memory of the three conspiracies, or covins, that rose up against the Stone Lords, and the witches who led each one;
E	were once the "Three Stars" of Tierstered, makerglass gems burning with eternal flame;
E	are <b>banefires</b> (page 42), each one imprisoning an undead sorcerer;
E	are spirit-catchers, enthralling ghosts and keeping them bound;
E	are ghostly hordes standing vigil over mass graves; or
E	are some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.

B	Someone aims to destroy the dam (draining the lake, flooding the Sruth, dooming Marshedge)
H2	Getting there
HR
P	To get there directly from Stonetop…
C	First you must travel to the Steplands, which will take at least 4 days.
C	From there, it will take at least 3 days and a corresponding amount of supplies.
C	You need a knowledgeable guide; but
C	Even then, you risk getting lost.
P	To get there from <b>Marshedge</b> (page 274), follow the River Sruth upstream to the lake, and…
C	It will take at least 4 days, and a corresponding amount of supplies; and
C	You need a knowledgeable guide or you risk getting lost.
P	Either way…
C	The terrain itself is treacherous, you risk injury on the way;
C	The way is grueling, you risk exhausting yourselves/your resources; or
C	The way is perilous, plagued with danger.
H2	Areas
B	<b>The Gwazhi:</b> A sizeable river that feeds the lake, flowing from the <b>Huffel</b> <b>Peaks</b> (page 236).
B	<b>Surrounding hills and valleys:</b> Once full of farms, mines, villages, manors. Site of many Barrow Builder battles.
B	<b>Western shores:</b> Where the Gwazhi enters the lake. Marshy, silty, gross. Frogs, birds, bugs.
B	<b>Northern shore:</b> Piles of boulders and a great looming bluff. Treacherous shorelines.
B	<b>Southern shore:</b> Gentler (but still rugged) shorelines, with smaller bluffs a ways back from the water.
B	<b>Eastern shore:</b> Deep water. Sheer bluffs joined by a Stone Lord dam.
B	<b>The Lake itself:</b> Shallow near shores but plenty of deep, open water. Hides many dangers and many treasures. Freezes over in winter.
PAGE	441
H2	Sites
HR
B	<b>The dam:</b> A mighty wall between two bluffs on the eastern shore. Granite blocks, mortared in place with makerglass. A huge pipe drains water into the river Sruth. Beware the <b>whirlpool</b> (page 445).
B	<b>Glassworks:</b> The westernmost bluff on the south shore, hollowed out. Partly collapsed, wholly looted, still full of cold, echoing furnaces and huge globs of makerglass.
B	<b>The Academy:</b> Part of the north bluff. Maker-sized dormitories, workshops, and lecture halls. Gutted and vandalized. Used by Barrow Builders as a fortress.
B	<b>Amphitheater:</b> Carved into a bluff, overlooking a large cove on the southern bank. Impossibly good acoustics. The site of countless bloody sacrifices.
B	<b>The Vault of Skol Paasco:</b> A large, rocky isle in the middle of the lake, a tower's foundation clearly visible. A heavily-warded makerglass door guards the untouched cellars.

P	1d12 stone lord site
HR
P	1 Sunken head of an enormous statue, coated in algae. Sings a haunting song each sunset.
P	2 Vaulted chamber, littered with pieces of an obsidian mirror once
P	30' across. Shards reflect brief vignettes of days long past.
P	3 Four-story "tower" carved out of a bluff. Crystals inside emanate light, awe, reverence.
P	4 Bluff-sized building of seamless stone. Inside, a warren of unstable, bone-strewn apartments.
P	5 Double doors, crudely barricaded.
P	Beyond: a cracked crystal, a broken ward, lingering evil.
P	6 Big island made mostly of huge, curving stone slabs. Alcoves hold signs of ancient refugee camps:
P	cookware, salvage, keepsakes.
P	7 Spiral stairs, rising 100' from a pile of rubble. Makerglass, giant- sized steps, draped in vines.
P	8 Big blocky building. Intact. Doors buried under rubble/scree. Holds a cache of spare construct parts.
P	9 Warren of rooms carved into a bluff. Once a Stone Lord's manor, then a warlord's fortress, finally the site of her demise.
P	10 Long stretches of narrow stone walkway, mostly buried by silt and shallow water. Covered in algae, mud, faded runes.
P	11 Rocky island far from shore, like a great hand holding a broken stone platter. Ancient (?) skulls are heaped on every surface.
P	12 Makerglass tower, largely intact but fallen sideways into the lake.
P	Full of wonders, algae, eels, stale air pockets, Stone Lord ghosts.
P	The above are just examples. See page 384 if you need to create more or different sites.
P	Most sites were <b>reclaimed</b> (page 36) by the Barrow Builders at some point.
P	Most sites around Three Coven Lake were long ago stripped of anything valuable. If a site contains some sort of treasure, there must be a reason. It could be…
E	inaccessible (buried, locked, flooded, well-hidden, etc.);
E	<b>corrupted</b> (page 430) by the power of the Things Below;
E	dangerously <b>haunted</b> (page 72);
E	protected by <b>constructs</b> (page 392), <b>perilous stone</b> (page 391), bound spirits, and/or other magic;
E	currently inhabited; or
E	some combination of the above.

H2	The portal of Teirstered
HR
P	Hidden away in some vault—guarded by constructs, traps, and spells of misdirection—there stands a slab of white stone, 40' by 40', inscribed with a circle of deep-cut runes.
P	The circle is a <b>portal</b> (page 306), connected to those in the <b>Ruined Tower</b> (page 332), the <b>Labyrinth</b> (page 242), <b>Vor Svetelik</b> (page 468), and so forth. It requires a power source. If one is provided, it can be used via <b>Opening the Way</b> (page 517).

B	Instinctive dread, from a generational fear of water
B	Steep, unexpected drop-offs
B	Poor footing (slick rocks, mud, plants and other snares)
B	Strong, often unseen currents
B	Choppy water, waves up to 4' on extremely windy days
B	Shivering cold, the threat of debilities or even <b>hypothermia</b> (page 489)
B	Getting dragged down by your own gear
B	The fact that they probably can't swim
P	See also: The <b>Blood-drunk Queen</b> (page 447).

H3	Drowning
P	When you <b><i>plunge beneath the water</i></b>, hold Breath equal to 1 + your CON. If you first took a deep breath, hold 2 extra
P	Breath.
P	When you <b><i>make a move while under water</i></b>, and that move involves a roll, choose 1 of the following after the move is resolved:
B	Spend 1 Breath
B	Mark a debility
B	Drop to 0 HP; you're drowning and soon to be at Death's Door
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Thin ice
P	The lake starts to freeze in early winter and thaws in early spring. It's usually frozen at least 4" thick (safe enough to walk on) by midwinter. But it doesn't freeze uniformly; it can be 2' thick in one place and just a few inches thick only a few yards away.
P	• Footsteps fall with a hollow noise
P	• Water/slush well up around your feet
P	• Something underfoot cracks, lurches
P	• SPLOOSH
P	Anyone falling through the ice risks panic and drowning. If they manage to escape, they're probably already suffering <b>hypothermia</b> (page 489).

H3	The whirlpool
P	Near the dam at the east edge of the lake, a great drain draws in water and empties it into the river Sruth. When one or more PCs get too close, start the following:
C	They're caught in the current
C	They're dragged closer, and can no longer swim/paddle free
C	Down the funnel they go
C	<b>Impending doom:</b> They are sucked into the pipe
P	When you <b><i>get sucked into the pipe</i></b>, take
P	1d10+2 damage with advantage (ignores armor) and roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, you get spat out into the river, alive but soaked and beaten (mark a debility); <b>on a 7-9</b>, you get spat out but mark a debility and lose 1d4 ◇ from your inventory and 1d4 small items; <b>on a 6-</b>, as a 7-9 but also you are at Death's Door.

H3	The Chained Beast
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>corrupted</i>, <i>aquatic</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 20; <b>Armor</b> 2 (fur and scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> toothy maw d10+3 w/advantage (<i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing) or raking claws d10+1 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> chained to a heavy block of makerglass, takes +1d6 damage from bronze, soothed by a well-sung song
P	<b>Instinct</b> to gorge itself
P	• Scent blood, anywhere in the lake
P	• Shoot through the water
P	• Snatch prey, pull it under
P	• Regenerate any wound not dealt by bronze
P	• Drag its mooring across the lakebed, slowly and painfully
P	It was a gift from the Things Below, a present to some Barrow Builder tyrant. They bound it fast and kept in the waters nearby, feeding it a steady of diet of screaming, bleeding victims. It's still out there, sleeping for years or decades at a time, roused by copious amounts of fresh blood in the lake—or by a few drops somewhere nearby.
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Screech eel
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>small</i>, <i>aquatic</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 3; <b>Armor</b> 1 (speed), 2 vs. attacks from above the water <b>Damage</b> tearing bite d6 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>,
P	1 piercing)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to feed on easy prey
P	• Slink up on potential prey
P	• Screech to attract other eels (barely heard above the water)
P	• Attack in a frenzied swarm, all bites and screeches and churning bloody water
P	About 5' or 6' long. They mostly prey on fish or fowl, hunting silently and by themselves. Somehow, though, they learned that people are delicious. Too big for one eel to tackle, sure. But people in the water are clumsy and oblivious. So when a screech eel spots someone in the water, it calls out to its friends. And when enough of them have gathered, they feast.

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	The Blood-drunk Queen
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to slake her thirst for violence and suffering
P	• Appear in dreams, or to those who are drowning: a gaunt and longlimbed queen, her mouth stained crimson
P	• Wash up a secret/treasure, to tempt fools or stir up violence
P	• Turn the lake against those who have not appeased her
P	The lake has always had a spirit. A fickle goddess, beautiful and bountiful, sometimes harsh and greedy. But then the walkway-seal was broken, and horror seeped into the waters. Then the multitudes were drowned, and the goddess drank their deaths. Then came generations of violence, and she lapped up all the blood that was spilled.
P	When you <b><i>make a bloody offering to the</i></b> <b><i>spirit of the lake</i></b>, roll and add…
E	+1 if you do it at a proper shrine;
E	+1 if the victim dies in agony & fear; and
E	+1 if you spill the lifeblood of a human-sized creature, or +2 if you spill substantially more than that.
P	<b>On a 7+</b>, you have appeased the spirit of the lake and She will not actively torment you or your companions (for this visit, at least). Also, <b>on a 10+</b>, hold 2 Preparation (per the Bolster move), which you or a companion can spend on any roll related to exploring or navigating the lake, or facing its dangers.
